fallback.text: A journey from Rome to Alexandria on a network of Roman roads, coastal hops and sea lanes. In July the fastest route goes by road to Ostia (30 km) and then across the open sea, about 2 150 km: some 17.6 days with ships making 130 km a day. In January the open sea is closed (mare clausum), so the traveller goes by road to Brundisium and then along the coasts by Corinth, Rhodes and Caesarea: six stages, about 3 030 km and 45 days. The straight geodesic distance is 1 953 km, about 1 320 Roman miles.
